100.title: Core Learning Policy — ทุก Bug/Duplicate/Drift ที่พบต้องบันทึกเป็นบทเรียนใน registry/existence.json known_mistakes ก่อนถือว่าจบงาน ห้ามเก็บไว้เฉพาะ AI conversation (CONST-100, DNA-000026)
100.detection: mixed — KM-002-class findings (duplicate module/basename) mechanically WARNed by Guard 9; other classes (e.g. KM-001, duplicated parsing logic) documented with cross-reference comments, no mechanical check exists yet — see registry/existence.json known_mistakes[].detection for the honest per-entry status
100.canonical_id: C-006 (Every resolved incident must become reusable knowledge)

101.title: Connect before Create, Compose before Expand — ก่อนสร้าง capability/registry/runtime/explanation-engine ใหม่ ต้องตรวจสอบก่อนว่ามีของเดิมที่ทำหน้าที่นี้อยู่แล้วหรือไม่ ห้ามสร้างซ้ำ (CONST-101, DNA-000030)
101.detection: mixed, stated honestly — the module/file-basename layer of 'no duplicate' is mechanically enforced (same Guard 9 / KM-002 / confirmed_duplicate_pairs infrastructure Rule 100 built, DNA-000027). The broader instruction ('search for an existing capability/registry/runtime/explanation-engine before building a new one') has no mechanical gate — nothing scans intent or purpose, only file names and import edges. Compliance today depends on whoever is building (human or AI) actually running discovery first (e.g. npm run hello, a registry read) — same as SDRN-P1/P2 did in practice before this rule was written down. Not claiming automated enforcement that doesn't exist.

102.title: Self Publishing Runtime Protocol (SPRP) — ทุก Runtime Component ต้องรับผิดชอบการประกาศการมีอยู่ของตัวเอง (identity/capability/state/health/dependency/resource/owner/execution-status/improvement-request) เชิงรุก ห้ามให้ AI ค้นพบด้วยการไล่อ่าน source code (CONST-102, DNA-000031)
enforced_by: core/shared/types.ts (RuntimeContract 19-field type, NegotiationFlowState, computeNegotiationStage — SDRN-P6, DNA-000060)
plugins/drivers/line.selfDescription.ts (getLineDriverRuntimeContract — full 19-field real implementation, 2nd real module)
core/shared/types.ts (ContextBudget, DeltaContext, WorkOrder, ExecutionReadiness, VerificationContract, MeasurementReport + real derivation functions — SDRN-P7, DNA-000061)
core/runtime/contextBroker.ts (SDRN-P8, DNA-000062 — real compute-once/cache/reuse broker, real read counter)
core/runtime/contextBroker.ts (ExecutionReport + generateExecutionReport — real aggregation, no new computation)
102.detection: NOT mechanical. Recorded honestly as a declared engineering target, not an enforced rule. Real coverage today: engines/documents/selfDescription.ts implements the 'describe on demand' half of this (SelfDescribe(), SDRN-P1) for exactly 1 of 466 modules; scripts/hello.ts is the one real place anything gets composed/published, and only on manual invocation (npm run hello), not proactively/continuously. The Publish*() interface family (PublishState/PublishHealth/PublishNeed/PublishDependency/PublishCapability/PublishKnowledge/PublishWarning/PublishProposal), inter-component negotiation, and continuous self-reporting do not exist anywhere in this codebase. The closest existing prior art — per Rule 101, checked before writing this entry rather than assumed — is core/workspace/runtimeRegistry.ts (register/unregister/getStatus/list/subscribe, a real pub/sub-shaped primitive already built for the Visual Workspace canvas), but register() is called nowhere in the app (confirmed multiple times this session) and it only covers state, not the other 8 Publish* categories. Building SPRP for real would mean extending that existing primitive, not creating a second one — and is Feature-scale work requiring its own Plan Lock exception and phased scope, same as SDRN-P1/P2, not something this rule entry itself performs. UPDATE (DNA-000059): the real implementation (engines/documents/selfDescription.ts) now covers all 9 C-011 fields — added `constraints` and `verificationProcedure` (previously absent from core/shared/types.ts's SelfDescription interface entirely) plus `missingKnowledge` (distinct from the pre-existing `missing`), verified live via a direct tsx invocation returning real, non-fabricated values for all 3. Still true: only 1 of ~470 registered modules has any SelfDescription implementation at all — this closes a field-completeness gap for that one module, it does not extend coverage to more modules. UPDATE (DNA-000060, SDRN-P6): the full 19-field RuntimeContract (Identity/Purpose/Responsibilities/Capabilities/Dependencies/Constraints/Health/Current State/Known Problems/Missing Knowledge/Missing Capabilities/Missing Dependencies/Resources Needed/Requested Actions/Execution Scope/Forbidden Scope/Verification Procedure/Success Criteria/Confidence/Last Validation) plus a real, pure computeNegotiationStage() function now exist as real types/code — verified live via direct tsx invocation for 2 real modules (Document Engine, LINE driver), both returning genuinely computed (not fabricated) values, including a correctly-computed 'knowledge_gap' negotiation stage for both (Document Engine: unwired Capability Orchestrator chain + no versioning scheme; LINE driver: no automated functional test for the AppleScript automation). Still true: only 2 of ~470 registered modules have any RuntimeContract implementation — this was an explicit, scoped Plan Lock exception (SDRN-P6), not a repo-wide rollout, and the owner's stated end-goal (contract-first replacing repository-first discovery for all future AI sessions) remains a declared target, not something now mechanically enforced for AI behavior in general. UPDATE (DNA-000061, SDRN-P7): real Contract Coverage measured live — 2 of 473 registered modules (0.42%). The other 6 named metrics (Repository Read Count, Context Size, Context Reuse Ratio, Delta Context Ratio, Repository Scan Avoidance, Execution Preparation Time) are real TYPES with honest null values and a stated unmeasurableReason — this repository has no access to AI session token/read/timing data, which lives in the Claude Code harness outside this repo. Per the owner's own explicit instruction, no numeric reduction is claimed. ExecutionReadiness/ContextBudget/DeltaContext/WorkOrder are real, computed, and verified live for the same 2 modules — explicitly advisory only, nothing mechanically gates AI execution on these values. UPDATE (DNA-000062, SDRN-P8): real before/after measurement now exists and was run live — 55 real repository reads (independent recomputation) vs 11 real repository reads (broker, cached) for the same 2-module repeated-access workload, an 80% real, computed reduction (not estimated). Precisely scoped: this measures the broker's own internal behavior only, not an AI session's overall token/read behavior, which remains outside this repository's observability. UPDATE (DNA-000063, SDRN-P9): after auditing a 10-item 'Runtime Knowledge Platform' directive against real state (3 items already built, 1 overlapping knip/jscpd, several not achievable — mechanical repository-access gating and AI-reasoning caching are not data this repo can observe or store), the owner confirmed a narrowed scope. ExecutionPlan/ExecutionReport built and verified live for both real modules across a real cache-miss and cache-hit — repositoryReads correctly stayed flat and executionTimeMs correctly dropped to 0 on the cache hit, confirming real, not fabricated, behavior. UPDATE (DNA-000064, SDRN-P10): RuntimePacket now includes briefing (real synthesis) and architecture (real module-registry.json/dependency-graph.json lookup). A real bug was caught and fixed live in this same pass — architecture's first implementation added real file reads even on a cache hit, contradicting the already-verified 0-additional-reads claim; fixed by caching it alongside the contract, re-verified (8 reads unchanged across a cache-hit access).
102.canonical_id: C-011 (Every module must be self-describing; no AI may inspect implementation before reading self-description)

103.title: Reuse Before Build — ก่อนสร้าง module/registry/runtime/database/API/workflow/event bus/cache/service/interface/storage ใหม่ใด ๆ ต้องค้นหาก่อนว่ามี implementation เดิมอยู่แล้วหรือไม่ ทุก request ต้องได้ข้อสรุปเป็นหนึ่งใน 3: EXISTING (ใช้ของเดิม) / EXTEND (ต่อยอดของเดิม) / NEW (สร้างใหม่ เฉพาะเมื่อพิสูจน์แล้วว่าไม่มีของเดิมที่ใช้ได้) ทุกบรรทัดโค้ดใหม่ต้องอธิบายได้ว่าทำไมโค้ดเดิมแก้ปัญหานี้ไม่ได้ (CONST-103, DNA-000036)
103.detection: Mechanical only at the same narrow layer Rule 101 already covers — module/file-basename duplication (Guard 9, confirmed_duplicate_pairs). The EXISTING/EXTEND/NEW decision framework itself has no mechanical check — nothing in this codebase can algorithmically determine whether a proposed capability semantically overlaps 80%+ with an existing one; that judgment is currently made by whoever is building (human or AI) actually searching first. Real, lived evidence this rule already describes existing practice rather than inventing new behavior: every SDRN-P1 through P5 phase this session applied exactly this EXISTING/EXTEND/NEW test before writing code (e.g. SDRN-P3 found core/workspace/runtimeRegistry.ts already existed and extended it instead of building a second registry; SDRN-P5 built on engines/documents/selfDescription.ts instead of a new interface file; the persistence-model decision was deferred rather than building a new event bus without evidence one was needed). Not claiming this makes the discipline automatic — it documents that it has been followed manually, consistently, and gives it a rule number so future sessions (human or AI) are held to the same standard explicitly rather than by accumulated precedent alone.

104.title: Nothing Is Wasted — ก่อนลบ source code ใด ๆ ต้อง extract ความรู้ก่อนเสมอ (purpose/owner/dependencies/failure reason/replacement/migration path/lessons learned) ทุก implementation ที่ retire แล้วต้องกลายเป็น Runtime Knowledge (registry/existence.json) และห้ามสร้าง implementation ใหม่ที่ recreate mistake ที่เคย archive ไว้ — ทุกการ REJECT ต้องอ้างอิง knowledge จริงที่เป็นเหตุผล ไม่ใช่แค่ชี้ไปที่ไฟล์เฉย ๆ (CONST-104, DNA-000037/038/039/040)
104.type: declarative + real mechanical enforcement for 2 of 4 known cases
104.detection: Mechanical for 3 real things: (1) build-arch-book.ts only excuses a module from UNUSED via archival_status:"ARCHIVED" if archived_knowledge_ref resolves to a real entry — verified by testing a fake ref, confirmed BROKEN, restored (DNA-000038). (2) Guard 10 (pre-commit-check.sh) hard-REJECTs if a new file recreates the basename of an already-archived module, AND its rejection message resolves and prints the real matched archived_knowledge entry's id/failure_reason/replacement_successor directly — not just a generic pointer at the file (DNA-000040, verified by copying an archived file to a new path and confirming the printed AK-001 id, real failure_reason text, and real replacement_successor path). Deliberately excludes conventional/repeated-by-design basenames (index.ts, engine.ts, etc., same list Guard 9 already excludes) — 2 of the 4 currently-archived files (engines/impact/engine.ts, core/auth/index.ts) have exactly this basename-genericity problem and were excluded after a dry run proved they'd otherwise hard-reject the repo's own real, unrelated files (10+ real engine.ts, 30+ real index.ts). Those 2 remain fully documented and searchable, just not eligible for the recreation-check specifically. (3) npm run hello -- --archive <query> makes archived_knowledge searchable by keyword. STILL NOT mechanical: nothing intercepts a real `rm` before knowledge extraction happens (no pre-write/pre-delete hook exists in this toolchain, stated honestly since DNA-000037) — Rule 104's item 9 ("reject permanent deletion until knowledge extraction succeeds") is real only in the sense that build-arch-book.ts would flag a deleted-but-never-archived module as UNUSED/BROKEN after the fact, not that deletion itself is blocked.

105.title: Autonomous Architecture Maintenance Authorization — Runtime/AI may modify without re-asking approval when all 4 conditions hold (existing-rules-compliant, no business-logic change, scope limited to maintenance/sync/repair/metadata/dependency-correction/docs/validation/tooling, passes all validators before+after); every autonomous change must record executor/timestamp/affected modules-files-functions/reason/root cause/validation before-after/rollback into CHANGELOG.json + VALIDATION_RESULTS.json + CURRENT_STATE.json; exceeding Constitution scope means stop and create an Owner Task instead (CONST-105, DNA-000052)
enforced_by: registry/CHANGELOG.json (autonomous_execution audit block on each qualifying entry)
105.type: declarative + real audit-trail mechanism, no scope-eligibility guard
105.detection: Mechanical for the AUDIT TRAIL itself once a change is underway: scripts/record-validation.ts already writes real before/after PASS/FAIL records (reused, not duplicated); CHANGELOG.json entries can carry a real autonomous_execution object (first real instance: DNA-000052 itself, the governance.sh jscpd --exitCode->--exit-code fix). NOT mechanical: whether a proposed change actually qualifies under the 4 conditions (especially condition 2, "does not change Business Logic") is judged by the executing AI itself — no guard inspects a diff and rejects it for being out of the autonomous-maintenance scope before it happens. This is a real, stated gap, same honesty pattern as Rules 101-104.

106.title: Runtime Self-Evolving Knowledge Layer — repair must never end at the file edit; every fix requires real root-cause analysis, a check for existing Detection capability, new Detection/Diagnostic/Explanation/Validation/Dependency/Architecture capability if missing (connected to existing systems, never a parallel one), a re-test that the same incident is now caught automatically, a Deploy Gate blocking on real Runtime Validation PASS with a human-readable explanation on FAIL, immediate Knowledge/Root-Cause/Validation Engine recording, and Capability-building (not another point fix) on a 3rd recurrence of the same incident (CONST-106, DNA-000053)
enforced_by: scripts/deploy-gate.ts (DNA-000053, step 5 — real, tested, blocks with a human-readable explanation)
package.json prebuild hook (DNA-000055 — actually wired into npm run build, not just built)
registry/VALIDATION_RESULTS.json + scripts/record-validation.ts (DNA-000050/051 — real Validation Engine recording)
registry/existence.json known_mistakes (Knowledge/Root-Cause Engine recording, e.g. KM-004, KM-005)
106.type: declarative + real mechanical enforcement for step 5 (Deploy Gate) only
106.detection: Mechanical only for step 5 (deploy blocked on real Validation FAIL, verified live multiple times this session). Steps 1-4, 6 are the discipline this session has actually followed manually each time (root-cause analysis, detection-gap checking, capability-building, re-testing, knowledge recording) but have no mechanical check that an AI actually DID all of them before declaring a fix complete — the Root Cause Engine Output Contract (registry/EXECUTION_CONTRACT.json, DNA-000057) is the closest thing to enforcement, and it too is a stated requirement, not a mechanical gate. Step 7 (3rd-occurrence escalation) is still a manual discipline (KM-001's 3 recurrences leading to Guard 11 is the one real precedent), no automatic recurrence counter exists. UPDATE (DNA-000065): the owner's 18-dimension Operational Intelligence Objective (8 reduce / 10 increase) was mapped against real, current coverage, not assumed. Real finding: 4 of the 8 'reduce' dimensions and effectively 0 of the 'increase' dimensions beyond what's already listed above have NO real mechanical tracking today — structural ambiguity, business ambiguity, duplicate workflow, and duplicate data access have zero real checks anywhere in this repository (confirmed directly: scripts/check-workflow-coverage.sh checks completeness, not duplication; no duplicate-data-access checker exists). The rest of the 18 dimensions have real, evidence-based partial-to-full coverage already built across Rules 100/101/103/104/105/107/108/109/110 and SDRN-P6 through P10 — see the Rule 106 amendment text for the full per-dimension mapping.
106.canonical_id: C-006 (Every resolved incident must become reusable knowledge)

107.title: Evidence Isolation — audit tools must never scan ledger/report/log/validation files as if they were source; runtime-generated evidence must never re-enter the same or next audit cycle as input (CONST-107, DNA-000056/057)
enforced_by: scripts/governance.sh (jscpd invocations explicitly scoped to typescript/tsx, ignoring **/*.json)
107.type: declarative + real mechanical fix for the 2 known real violators
107.detection: Mechanical only for the specific tools already fixed (Guard 1's grep, jscpd in governance.sh/dashboard.sh) — verified live by resetting the ledger and re-running a real subprocess, confirming zero VALIDATION_RESULTS.json matches and a stable clone count across two consecutive runs. NOT mechanical: no general-purpose check scans every audit tool invocation across scripts/*.sh and verifies it excludes the known Evidence Zone (VALIDATION_RESULTS.json, CHANGELOG.json, DNA_OS_HEALTH.json) — a new tool added later could reintroduce this exact failure mode undetected.
107.canonical_id: C-001, C-002, C-003 (Evidence is never Source; generated files never re-enter the pipeline; audit boundaries must be explicit)

108.title: Tool Invocation & Configuration Precedence Contract — CLI > Environment > Config File; every real CLI override of a config file must be logged at the override site, not silent (CONST-108, DNA-000056/057)
enforced_by: scripts/governance.sh (jscpd line carries an inline comment documenting the override)
108.detection: NOT mechanical — the only 2 known real overrides (jscpd CLI args silently beating .jscpd.json) were found by manual evidence inspection during a live audit, then fixed and commented. No tool compares a script's actual CLI invocation against its target's config file to flag divergence automatically; a future CLI change could silently override config again without detection.
108.canonical_id: C-003, C-004, C-008 (explicit audit boundary; deterministic tool invocation; no silent governance override)

109.title: Environment Verification Before Audit — must confirm grep/sed/awk/tail/tr resolve to real binaries, not shell wrappers, before trusting audit results; interactive-shell test results are not proof of real subprocess behavior (CONST-109, DNA-000056/057)
109.type: real mechanical check, run manually — not yet auto-invoked
109.detection: Mechanical: scripts/verify-environment.sh checks `type grep/sed/awk/tail/tr` for each and WARNs if any resolves to anything other than a plain file path. NOT yet wired into governance.sh/pre-commit-check.sh/deploy-gate.ts's automatic run — must be invoked manually (npm run verify-env) until wired in, so it does not yet prevent this failure mode from recurring silently in a fresh environment.
109.canonical_id: C-005 (Environment must be verified before execution)

110.title: Encoding Contract — no raw byte-offset truncation (tail -c N) feeding into a UTF-8-validating command (tr) without multi-byte protection; use LC_ALL=C or equivalent (CONST-110, DNA-000056/057)
enforced_by: scripts/governance.sh (LC_ALL=C tr fix, the one known real instance)
110.type: real fix for the 1 known real violator, no general check
110.detection: Mechanical only for the one specific line fixed — verified live (bash governance.sh as a real subprocess, zero 'Illegal byte sequence' occurrences, confirmed by grep -c on the real output). NOT mechanical: no check scans scripts/*.sh for the `tail -c ... | tr` pattern generally; a new script reintroducing this exact pattern would not be caught automatically.

111.title: Extend Capability, Never Duplicate Pipeline — owner commands by outcome ("เพิ่ม X"); AI must treat this as Extension of the existing system by default, never Replacement, unless owner explicitly signals a core change (CONST-111, 2026-07-17)
enforced_by: registry/intent-dictionary.json (Phase 0 — records known intents, known_implementations, and invariant_compliance per implementation; human/AI-read reference, not yet a mechanical gate)
111.type: process/behavioral rule — no mechanical enforcement exists yet
111.detection: NOT mechanical. No pre-commit guard or script scans for a new file/route that duplicates an existing registered intent — compliance today depends entirely on whoever is building (human or AI) reading registry/intent-dictionary.json first. This is the same honest limitation already documented under Rule 101/103 ("nothing scans intent or purpose, only file names and import edges"); Rule 111 names the failure mode explicitly, it does not yet close the gap. A real Intent Guard (Phase 3 of the Execution Registry initiative) is planned but not built.

112.title: AI Memory Is Not Source of Truth — an AI's own working memory (CLAUDE.md/MEMORY.md/feedback_*.md or equivalent) may explain and remember, but rules must always derive from registry/CONSTITUTION.json, never originate in AI memory (CONST-112, 2026-07-17)
112.detection: NOT mechanical. Nothing in this codebase verifies that an AI memory file's stated rules trace back to a real Constitution rule number — compliance depends on the AI itself (or a human reviewer) checking. Stated honestly as a discipline, not a claim of automated enforcement, matching this file's existing convention for process rules (e.g. Rule 101/103's own coverage notes).

113.title: Document Immutability — sent invoices are fixed once issued; corrections happen via Void + reissue (new number), never in-place edit. Debt Reminder is a snapshot, not a tax document; Receipt only on confirmed real payment; Tax Invoice only on a real taxable transaction (CONST-113, 2026-07-18)
113.detection: NOT mechanical. app/api/admin/documents/[id]/route.ts's PATCH handler currently allows editing an invoice's subtotal/vat_rate/total_amount regardless of invoice_status (sent invoices are NOT currently protected from in-place edits at the code level) — this rule is a declared discipline, not yet a guard. Stated honestly per this file's existing convention for process rules.

114.title: Documents Are Derived From Business Events, Not Button Clicks — a document is created only from a real business event (sale/payment/cancellation); if an active, not-yet-superseded document already exists for the same partner+debt, reuse/resend it instead of creating a new one (CONST-114, 2026-07-18)
114.detection: NOT mechanical. engines/documents/draft-builders.ts's buildDraftFromPartner() and app/api/admin/documents' POST handler currently have no check for an existing active invoice before creating a new one — confirmed by a real incident (INV-20260717-352 void -> INV-20260718-649, same underlying debt, one day apart). Stated honestly as a declared discipline pending a real idempotency check, not a claim of automated enforcement.

115.title: Payment Verification Priority Levels — payment_verified only becomes true once every currently-real verification level (LINE claim, OCR slip, and eventually bank email/statement) agrees; human confirmation stands in for the still-unbuilt Level 3/4 (CONST-115, 2026-07-18)
enforced_by: app/api/admin/receipt-documents/[id]/confirm/route.ts (sets payment_verified=true only on real human confirmation)
115.type: runtime (partial) — the level-1/level-2 tagging and the human-confirmation gate are real code; Level 3/4 themselves do not exist
115.detection: Real for what exists today: verification_level is set mechanically by the code paths listed, and payment_verified cannot become true without a human hitting the confirm endpoint. NOT mechanical for the full 4-source cross-check the rule describes — bank email and bank statement/API integrations are confirmed absent from this codebase (see registry/CHANGELOG.json's Payment Verification Engine Phase 1 entries), so Level 3/4 are declared, not built. Stated honestly per this file's convention.

116.title: Workspace Lock Manager & Dependency-Gated Migration — every registry/type edit should go through Lock Manager + Dependency Registry before commit; every resource move must be blocked the instant a real dependent is found (CONST-116, 2026-08-04)
enforced_by: supabase/migrations/20260804000005_workspace_lock_manager.sql (workspace_locks_active_resource_idx — real Postgres partial unique index, atomic)
engines/workspace/lockManager.ts (acquireLock/withLock — real DB-backed acquire, proven live: concurrent acquires for the same path only ever have one winner)
engines/storage/engine.ts's moveSafeToTrash() (calls createMigrationPlan() as a hard pre-check — real dependents force state BLOCKED, no override path)
116.type: runtime (partial) — lock atomicity and the storage-intelligence move pre-check are real, verified code. The 'no direct file writes' half of the rule is discipline-based, not mechanical.
116.detection: Real for what exists today: two concurrent workspace_locks INSERTs for the same resource_path can only have one succeed (Postgres-enforced), and engines/storage/engine.ts cannot move a file with a real dependent found in registry/architecture-book.json or registry/infra-dependency-graph.json. NOT mechanical: nothing in this repository can intercept a different AI session's or a human's direct Edit/Write tool call, or a plain text editor, bypassing engines/workspace/registryWriter.ts entirely — this is the same honest boundary Rule 105/108 already document. Stated per this file's convention, not overclaimed.

117.title: Development Machine Policy — no Production AI Runtime or model on the dev Mac; real drift check every 6h, alerts the owner via LINE when found (CONST-117, 2026-08-04)
enforced_by: engines/workspace/architectureDriftDetector.ts (real lsof/ps process check, real fs.existsSync for ~/.ollama and .gguf/.safetensors files, real grep of local-runtime scripts for live localhost:11434 fetch() calls)
local-runtime/storage-threshold-watcher.ts (calls detectArchitectureDrift() every 6h via the existing LaunchAgent, writes architecture_drift_events, posts to architecture-drift-alert when not clean)
117.type: runtime (partial) — the 4 known drift signals (local process, ~/.ollama, model weight files, live script references) are mechanically checked and alerted; broader Local AI Runtime shapes are not.
117.detection: Real for what's checked: verified live both directions via local-runtime/architecture-drift-acceptance-test.ts (clean machine reports clean; a synthetic violation with a real fetch() call to localhost:11434 is caught and classified). NOT mechanical for local AI runtimes outside the known pattern set (different port, different tool, no localhost:11434 literal) — stated honestly, not claimed as universal coverage.
